Question: Can you fine-tune models on structured and unstructured enterprise data? Describe integration with analytics platforms (Databricks, Snowflake). Are fine-tuned models registrable in governance?
Response: Our architecture prioritises skill crystallisation over model fine-tuning — proven patterns become deterministic code (skills), which is faster, cheaper, easier to govern, and easier to reverse. That said, fine-tuning is fully supported via two paths, and critically WPP's existing analytics models stay where the data lives — no migration required. (1) WPP's existing fine-tuned analytics models remain in-place: Databricks (MLflow + Model Serving) and Snowflake (Snowpark Container Services / Cortex). These are exposed as MCP tools through APIM AI Gateway, so agents invoke them where they already live. Mosaic AI Gateway (Databricks) and Snowflake Cortex are callable as MCP through APIM — a Databricks-hosted model call is governed identically to a Foundry model call (auth injection, rate limiting, content safety, audit). Unity Catalog fine-grained access control is preserved through OneLake shortcut federation. This directly addresses the §6.3 Advanced requirement for 'Fine-tuneable analytics models to run Analytics agents on structured and unstructured data (Databricks, Snowflake, file stores)' without model relocation. (2) For agent-specific fine-tuning (narrow-domain language, specialised document extraction), Azure AI Foundry provides fine-tuning workflows for models in the Foundry catalog. Training data can be sourced from Databricks + Snowflake via MCP connectors and OneLake shortcuts without migration. Fine-tuned models are registered in the Foundry model registry with full metadata (training data provenance, base model, fine-tuning parameters, evaluation results). All three registries (Databricks MLflow, Snowflake, Foundry) are governed identically via APIM.
Key Technologies: Azure AI Foundry fine-tuning, Foundry model registry, Databricks MLflow + Model Serving (MCP), Snowflake Snowpark + Cortex (MCP), Mosaic AI Gateway (MCP), OneLake shortcuts, Unity Catalog, Microsoft Fabric IQ (federation)
POC Demo: POC2: demonstrate Databricks MLflow model called as MCP tool by Hiring Agent's compensation benchmarking skill — model stays in Databricks under Unity Catalog governance; APIM mediates and audits.

Question: Can agents create, test, and provision data pipelines (not just consume them)? Describe support for orchestration tools (Prefect, dlt) and managed services (ADF, BigQuery).
Response: Yes. MAF agent executors (GHCP SDK sessions) can generate data pipeline definitions as part of their reasoning. The agent executor can: (1) Generate pipeline code (Python/SQL) for data transformation and analysis. (2) Test the pipeline in a sandboxed environment. (3) Submit for human review via the crystallisation pipeline. (4) Once approved, the pipeline is deployable to Azure Data Factory, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, or Snowflake via their respective APIs. MCP servers wrap ADF, Fabric, Databricks (SQL Warehouse, MLflow), and Snowflake (Snowpark, Cortex) pipeline APIs for agent-driven provisioning. OneLake shortcuts enable zero-copy federation — pipelines operate in-place on Databricks + Snowflake data; no ETL to Fabric is required unless the use case specifically benefits. For orchestration tools: Prefect and dlt are Python-native and can be invoked from agent executors. The code interpreter sandbox supports running pipeline code directly.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK (pipeline code generation), Azure Data Factory, Microsoft Fabric, Databricks, Snowflake, OneLake shortcuts, sandbox execution

Question: Can agents perform analytical reasoning over tabular data, generate visualisations, and produce insights without requiring a separate analytics tool?
Response: Yes. GHCP SDK sessions inside MAF agent executors reason over tabular data natively — the model performs quantitative analysis, anomaly detection, and insight generation as part of its reasoning chain. Agents can also invoke WPP's existing fine-tuned analytics models where they live: Databricks MLflow / Model Serving (via Mosaic AI Gateway as MCP) and Snowflake Cortex / Snowpark (as MCP) — enabling specialised analytics (compensation benchmarking, anomaly detection, predictive models) without moving models or data. For visualisations: the code interpreter sandbox generates charts and plots (Python matplotlib/plotly) which are included in workflow outputs and Control Plane displays (rendered via AG-UI components). Examples: (1) Budget Agent queries Workday + Databricks (via OneLake shortcut + MCP), generates cost impact analysis with visualisation. (2) End-of-workflow ROI report with cost/value charts on Control Plane. (3) Compensation benchmark analysis — agent invokes a Databricks-hosted levelling model via MCP, then an anomaly-detection Snowflake Cortex model via MCP. The Control Plane UI renders outputs via AG-UI components dynamically emitted by the agent executor.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK (analytical reasoning), Python code interpreter (visualisations), Databricks MLflow (MCP), Snowflake Cortex (MCP), Control Plane UI (AG-UI rendering)
POC Demo: POC1: Show end-of-workflow cost analysis with per-invoice cost breakdown chart on Control Plane. POC2: Show Databricks-hosted levelling model + Snowflake Cortex anomaly detection called as MCP tools by Hiring Agent's compensation benchmarking.
